subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Sample Roasting: Testing Before Committing
description: A short lesson to help you apply Sample Roasting: Testing Before Committing.

hook.text: Before roasting a full batch, roasters test small samples (50–150 grams) to evaluate the green coffee's potential.

buildup.text: Sample roasters are tiny drum machines that produce consistent, standardized light roasts for cupping (professional tasting).

discovery.text: Cupping the sample reveals acidity, sweetness, body, and defects—information that guides the production roast profile.

twist.text: A coffee that cups brilliantly as a sample can still fail in production if the profile isn't translated well.

climax.text: The gap between sample and production roasting is where many roasters struggle. Scaling up isn't just multiplying numbers.

punchline.text: Small test, big decision. Every production batch starts as a 100-gram trial.

quiz.question: Why do roasters use sample roasting before production?
options: To evaluate the green coffee's potential and guide the production roast profile
